for Data Centers for a period not to exceed one-hundred-and-eighty (180) days from the effective date

legal_basis.from: Ordinance 1-2026; extended by a second emergency ordinance passed by Village Council in mid-June 2026 following a 2026-06-15 public hearing (exact ordinance number not confirmed in sources reviewed)
legal_basis.to: Ordinance 1-2026; extended by Ordinance 29-2026, passed June 15, 2026.
legal_basis.reason: The Supreme Court identifies the extension by number.

duration.from: 180 days (Ord. 1-2026, effective 2026-01-05 through 2026-07-04), extended a further 180 days by a second emergency ordinance passed mid-June 2026, effective 2026-07-05 through approximately 2027-01-02
duration.to: Original moratorium up to 180 days through July 4, 2026; Ordinance 29-2026 extends the pause for a period not exceeding 180 days from its effective date. The ordinance recital also refers to passage; the effective date and resulting end date require verification.
duration.reason: Section 7 and the recital use different anchors; the prior July 5 start and January end are not established.

current_end_date_iso.reason: The operative effective date and termination cannot be established from the reviewed sources.

current_status.from: Active (extended) as of 2026-09-23; the second 180-day moratorium, passed as an emergency on 2026-06-15, took effect 2026-07-05 and runs to about 2027-01-01. Bristolville 25 Developer/BHGH Properties' mandamus case remains pending in the Ohio Supreme Court (developer's June 18 motion to compel site-plan review undecided per WKBN). The moratorium committee's consultant presented proposed data center zoning standards to council; no vote yet. Council separately adopted a 180-day moratorium on small modular reactors and battery energy storage systems in July 2026.
current_status.to: The Ohio Supreme Court opinion decided October 20, 2026 denies the requested Bristolville/BHGH writ concerning site-plan review under premoratorium law and identifies the June 15 extension as Ordinance 29-2026. This disposition does not establish resolution of every legal issue or subsequent proceeding. The signed extension section 7 states a maximum 180 days from effectiveness, while its recital refers to passage. Actual effective anchor, operative endpoint and later action remain unresolved.
